title: Settle a crease-mode draft's anchors into the valleys: an active contour on the crease field, one undoable edit; then snap a click to the nearest valley
description:
User 2026-10-25, from the IMG_4112 pilot: an authored anchor sat on top of a crest near no curvature, so the crease path bent up to it and back into the groove; the user moved it into the valley by hand. In crease mode the tool keeps an authored anchor exactly where it was clicked.

1. Settle (first): a control row (stable action id) on a crease-mode draft (rings and bisectors) that slides each anchor a short distance across the groove to the lowest crease energy nearby, with a smoothness term so the ring stays a clean loop: an active contour on the surface with the crease field (the one shared surface_creases lookup) as its potential. Authored anchors move only within a small radius so the user's intent is kept; supporting anchors may move further. The whole settle is one undoable edit, and the reply/lastRow lists how far each anchor moved.
2. Snap (follow-on, same energy): in crease mode, a click within a few pixels of a crease valley places the anchor on the valley, as bisector ends snap onto walls; geodesic-mode clicks stay exact.
definition-of-done:
1. Settle moves off-valley anchors into the groove on a synthetic grooved tube and on the IMG_4112 case (the anchor near tail_segment_1_underside_left), within the radius limits, as one undo step; tests.
2. Click snap in crease mode lands on the valley; geodesic clicks unchanged; tests.
3. Ring fingerprints of existing saved rings unchanged (settle only runs when asked).
testing-plan:
1. mvn test.
2. Live on references/CRAW-81/IMG_4112.dsl: reopen the ring, settle, compare anchor positions with the user's hand-moved one.
